text:
ryan_support: Heads up — customer 'NovaPay' escalated: p95/p99 latency regressed after the 03:00 UTC deploy. They hit p99 ~1.8s on text-generation route; SLO is 300ms. Can SRE triage?

alex_chen: thanks. any recent config changes to continuous-batcher?

ryan_support: support logs point at a config tweak earlier in the day: batcher max_wait_ms increased from 8 -> 40 for cost optimization. ticket from infra mentioned trying to reduce GPU utilization.

maria_g: yikes. that’s a big jump. p99 often sensitive to wait windows. do we have trace ids or request ids from NovaPay?

ryan_support: attached sample request ids: req_7123, req_7199. I pulled metrics: before change (02:40) p99 ~430ms, after (03:10) p99 ~1.8s. p50 unaffected. charts: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc/continuous-batcher?orgId=1

alex_chen: can we repro locally with high arrival jitter? if batcher is waiting up to 40ms to fill groups, tails will balloon when traffic is bursty. repro plan: run a load test with poisson arrival and diff batcher.wait.

jordan_ml: adding context: model is 7B decoder, kv-cache warmup negligible. This looks like batching-induced queuing rather than model slowdown. also saw occasional very small batches at high concurrency which can increase per-token overhead.

sre_oncall_bot: deploy-bot detected config change: service=batcher-svc, change_id=chg_2026-03-12-1729, param="max_wait_ms: 8 -> 40"

alex_chen: immediate mitigation: rollback max_wait_ms to 8 for the NovaPay route and any on-prem dedicated lanes. Can someone push a rollback or hotfix?

ryan_support: requesting rollback now. tagging infra eng. @maria_g can you coordinate with infra?

maria_g: starting rollback, will route only NovaPay traffic to old batcher config via routing override. Doing a canary: 5% -> 50% -> 100%.

deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated: service=batcher-svc, config=rollback-maxwait-8, canary=5%

alex_chen: while rollback goes, we should capture a flamegraph of batcher threads and the request queuing histogram. any queue-depth metrics?

ryan_support: attaching extracted logs from the worker pod (snippet):
```
[03:08:13.224] batcher: enqueuing req=req_7123, now=0ms
[03:08:13.268] batcher: batch dispatched size=3 wait=40ms
[03:08:13.269] runtime: schedule exec
[03:08:13.470] model: token-gen end for req_7123 total=1701ms
```

jordan_ml: that shows wait=40ms but 1701ms total — likely many requests sat in per-request queue until batch dispatched plus serialization overhead for tiny batches. Also if a few big requests block GPU earlier in timeline it can cascade.

maria_g: canary at 50% now. p99 on NovaPay route dropped to ~520ms at 50% traffic. continuing to 100%.

deploy-bot: canary rollout updated: 50% -> 100%

maria_g: rollback to 8ms complete for NovaPay route. asking customer to verify.

ryan_support: customer confirms latency back to normal for their traffic: p99 ~450ms. they reported some 5xx spikes during the window, likely due to timeouts.

alex_chen: root cause summary candidate: increasing max_wait_ms from 8 -> 40ms raised per-request queuing latency and increased batch dispatch jitter under bursty arrival patterns, producing higher p95/p99 even though mean throughput improved and GPU efficiency slightly rose.

jordan_ml: proposed longer-term mitigations:
- implement adaptive max_wait based on instantaneous queue depth and request age
- enforce per-route max_wait caps (e.g., customer SLO overrides)
- add fast-path for low-latency customers to bypass batching or use tiny-batcher with smaller kernel overhead
- emit per-batch wait histograms, and per-request queuing_latency metric (tagged by customer)

maria_g: also recommend adding automatic rollback when p99 exceeds threshold after config change (kinda a safety net). we can wire into rollout pipeline.

alex_chen: agree. also add a small loadtest to CI that runs with poisson traffic and checks p99 trends for a few representative routes.

ryan_support: I logged the customer incident and included timeline + rollback. Ticket: INC-2026-0457. we'll follow up with NovaPay on compensation.

jordan_ml: quick repro snippet for devs to run locally (bash):
```
# simulate poisson arrivals with lambda = 200 req/s
python tools/poisson_load.py --rate 200 --duration 120 --route /v1/generate --max_wait_ms 40
```

alex_chen: notes for runbook update:
- when customer p95/p99 regresses after batcher config change: check batcher max_wait and per-route overrides first
- query grafana panels: batcher.wait_hist, batch_size_hist, request_queue_depth, model_exec_time
- if change found, do canary rollback and gather traces + logs (include sample request ids)
- communicate to support + customer with ETA

ryan_support: closing loop with NovaPay, they are satisfied for now. keeping ticket open for follow-up on adaptive batching feature.

maria_g: filing a short postmortem + action items: instrument per-customer queue latency, add canary guard for p99, add CI poisson test, implement per-route max_wait knob.

alex_chen: thanks all. lesson: optimizing for cost by lengthening wait windows can subtly blow up tails for bursty traffic. we need to balance unit economics with SLOs. :thumbsup:

sre_oncall_bot: Incident INC-2026-0457 moved to status=monitoring

ryan_support: tagging for visibility: @product-observability @infra-plumbing
